verdict.line: You lose if you trade autos into her charged W or chase her Bladesurge resets past the wave; you win if you land E before she engages and stack Hemorrhage before you commit R.

brief.thesis: Darius' whole win condition is a stand-still trade long enough to stack Hemorrhage to 5 and threaten the Noxian Guillotine execute, and Irelia's kit exists specifically to deny that: Bladesurge (Q) lets her reset off a minion instead of fighting, Defiant Dance (W) cuts the physical damage she takes mid-trade, and Flawless Duet (E) stuns you the moment you try to close the gap. The matchup is decided by whether you can force the fight during the windows her Q and W are both down, which is exactly what your E (Apprehend) pull is built to create.

theirWindow.when: her E (850 range) is up and W ready
theirWindow.what: She can stun you from outside your own E range (535) then chain into a charged W for a safe opener. Don't walk onto minions in open lane once Flawless Duet is off cooldown.

yourWindow.when: her Q and W are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Walk her down and land E (Apprehend) to pull her in; with no reset and no damage reduction available she has to fight you on your terms, so start stacking Hemorrhage immediately.

start.why: The measured favorite (50.4% over 1257 games, 85.8% pick) — the sustain and AD buy you the health bar to hold stand-still trades long enough to stack Hemorrhage instead of backing off.

boots.why: Best-performing boots here (50.4% over 1239 games, 86.3% pick) — flattens the auto-attack damage from her Ionian Fervor attack speed stacking as fights drag on.

core.why: The active haste and movement close the gap onto a kiting Irelia so your E pull actually connects instead of whiffing on a repositioned target.
Stacking move speed lets you keep pace through a skirmish and armor holds up in the extended trades this matchup is built around.
Heals back the chip damage from her on-hit and poke over a long trade, buying the extra seconds needed to reach max Hemorrhage stacks.

situational.when: she's burst-diving you before you can stack Hemorrhage to max
she keeps resetting Bladesurge onto minions and you can't close the distance
the enemy team is stacking magic damage alongside her

runes.keystoneWhy: The higher-winrate page (52.1% over the sample) and it rewards exactly what this lane demands — sustained damage and healing the longer a trade runs. Master-tier Darius players instead run Stormraider's Surge (Sorcery) across 8,832 games; that suits a more mobile, hit-and-run playstyle that leans on Ghostblade resets rather than full stand-still fights.

summoners.why: Highest measured winrate and pick rate in this matchup (51.3%, 61.7% pick) — Ghost is what closes the distance on a champion whose whole kit is built to create separation from a dash-less Darius.

playing.title: Trade when Q and W are down
playing.detail: Bladesurge resets her position and Defiant Dance cuts incoming physical damage mid-charge; neither is available means neither escape nor damage reduction is available, so commit here.

playing.title: Land E before you swing
playing.detail: Apprehend (range 535, cooldown 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s) pulls her in and passively shreds a percentage of her Armor, so getting the hook off first makes every following auto and Q hit harder.

playing.title: Respect the 850-range stun
playing.detail: Flawless Duet (E, cooldown 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) stuns and Marks from further out than your own E reaches. Don't stand on minions in open lane once it's off cooldown.

playing.title: Don't auto into a charged W
playing.detail: Defiant Dance deals more damage the longer she holds it and reduces the physical damage she takes while charging. Back off and let the charge expire before you commit autos.

playing.title: Stack before you ult
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine's true damage scales per Hemorrhage stack, so land Q and autos to build toward 5 stacks before spending R rather than opening with it.

playing.title: Chain kills with R's reset
playing.detail: A killing Guillotine refreshes its own cooldown briefly (down to 6s at max rank), so after securing a kill in a skirmish immediately look for a second target instead of resetting to lane.

playing.title: Don't chase her Q resets
playing.detail: She can Bladesurge onto minions to disengage for free, so don't push past the wave chasing a fleeing Irelia — you'll just eat a stun on the way back.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and the win-rate/sample numbers above are measured from live OP.GG data on the current patch (76,458 Darius games overall, 1,192 in this specific matchup); the trade-timing and cooldown-window reasoning is my own read of the kits, not part of that dataset.

stats.opponentTip: Use [E] to pull Irelia while keeping in mind that she can use (Q) on minions to move around. Try to use your abilities when her (W) is on cooldown.
